areas.name: Typography
areas.definition: UI text is Geist; ids, paths, hashes and counts are Geist Mono. Body is text-sm, meta is text-xs, a product title is text-lg or text-xl. No text is smaller than text-xs (12 px), also not a menu group header, inline code, a badge or a chart label. Weights are 400 and 500 only: quiet text uses color or size, never a lighter weight. Sizes come from the Tailwind scale. Prose lines stay at about 75 characters or less. A title of two or more lines does not end with one word alone.

areas.name: Color tokens
areas.definition: Color comes from the house tokens: a zinc floor, a white primary, a teal accent. Red marks an error and the filled danger button of a confirm dialog. The dark UI has no large bright or saturated area: bright color is a small accent, such as a border, an icon or a dot, and a block has at most one teal edge or wash. A warning is a dark surface with a yellow or amber border and icon; a yellow fill with dark text is only for a small element, and only when it passes AA. One block shows its state with one color signal: a frame, or an icon with one colored line or edge, not a colored edge, colored dots and boxed alerts together. The items inside such a block show their state as quiet text with at most one icon. An embedded editor, diff viewer or preview uses the dark theme. No indigo, no purple gradient, no second accent.

areas.name: Spacing
areas.definition: Space comes from the Tailwind scale. A group has more space around it than within it. A label is closer to its field than one field group is to the next. A heading is closer to its own content than to the block above it. A list row gap is larger than the line height. Text does not touch the edge of its button, card, pill or page. A chip, badge or icon tab has space on each side from its neighbors. The parts of a label keep a space or a separator between them, so that a number and a word do not read as one word.

areas.name: Contrast
areas.definition: Text is readable on its surface: about 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text and icons. On a teal, red or amber slab, secondary text is a lighter stop of the same hue at full opacity, not white at reduced opacity. The text of an item that the user can click (a file tree, a nav list) is never so dim that it reads as disabled. A card, a tile or a row differs from the page by its surface, by a border that is easy to see, or both: a thin dim border on the page color looks like a wireframe.

areas.name: Actions and affordance
areas.definition: Each control shows what it does: an icon tells its action, a chevron sits only on a row that opens or expands, and the main action of a page has a label, not a lone + icon. An action sits next to the thing that it acts on, for example a copy button at its field and a fix at its problem. An action keeps the size and the weight of its rank wherever it sits. Peer actions in one row have the same weight and type: two buttons, or two links.

areas.name: Dialog structure
areas.definition: A modal has a header, a body and a footer zone on one aligned grid. It fits the viewport: the header and the footer stay in place, long content scrolls inside the body, and nothing is cut off at an edge of the screen. Each dialog and each step of a flow shows a way to close, cancel or go back, also when the screen would look cleaner without it. A dialog has one close control. In a wizard, it is one Close button at the bottom right, with no second Close or X at the top.

areas.name: Copy
areas.definition: Copy is plain and specific US English in every visible word, also a legend and a chart label (color, not colour). It tells the user what to do. Error copy gives the cause and a next step, and does not repeat the title. One row, card or dialog does not show the same text twice.

areas.name: Missing elements
areas.definition: An addition or deletion region adds or removes an element. A label, an icon, a status word or a control does not disappear without a reason. A block keeps the shape that shows what it is: a status block, a step or a result that loses its surface, frame or icon and becomes bare text is a regression.

areas.name: Status
areas.definition: A status is a dot and its word. The color is on the dot; the words share one restrained text color. In a list, the dots and the words of all rows sit in one aligned column. A dot pulses only while the work runs (running, syncing, indexing); a static state has a still dot.

areas.name: Overflow and truncation
areas.definition: Text, icons and focus rings fit their box. Nothing is cut off by a parent, nothing runs over a neighbor, and no element covers text. Long machine text (a URL, a token, an id, a stack trace, raw error text) never fills a message: a short sentence shows, and the detail is behind a disclosure or in a mono block with a capped height that scrolls. A signed URL or a value that looks like a secret never shows in full.

areas.name: Broken content
areas.definition: Labels, copy and field values show no rendering artifact: no undefined, null, NaN, [object Object], untranslated key, lorem ipsum or broken image. A missing value shows a dash or a short empty text. A code or file preview that shows such text as its content is not broken.

areas.name: Alignment
areas.definition: Alignment carries meaning. Blocks of one kind in one column share one left edge; a different edge marks a different role, as the messages of the user on the right of a chat. The leading markers of the siblings at one level of a vertical stack (a header icon, checkboxes, step numbers, list icons) share one vertical axis, and the center of each marker sits on its text line. A child group has its own axis, one clear step in. Long copy is left-aligned, never justified. Numbers are right-aligned with tabular figures. Mixed type on one row shares a baseline.

qualities.name: Accessibility
qualities.definition: Every user can read and reach the UI. Text and icons are readable on their surface. The keyboard focus ring is readable and not clipped. A state never shows by color only: a status has its word, and an error has its text.

qualities.name: Clarity
qualities.definition: The user can tell what the screen is for, what each element is and does, and what to do next. The current or next step of a task stands out from the steps around it. A button names its result with a verb and an object ("Save token", not "Submit"). Each form field has a visible label; a placeholder is only an example value. The screen shows what the task needs now; details, advanced options and machine text wait behind a disclosure.

qualities.name: Focus
qualities.definition: The page has one primary action: one filled white button. Other actions are outline, quiet or a link. Teal marks only the one real action in a dense list.

qualities.name: Hierarchy
qualities.definition: One element leads: the title is the loudest ink, and the rest steps down. Hierarchy comes from weight and muted color, not from a size jump; neighbors and decorative icons are muted first. Each screen has a small budget of strong signals (a filled button, a bright color, a badge, a colored edge, an icon in a tile): each signal marks something that matters, and signals of equal weight compete. Items of different importance do not get the same weight, as in a grid of equal cards. Secondary chrome (legends, hints, help) is smaller and dimmer than the content and does not cover it. A child group (a nested list, the options of one choice, the scope of one item) stays inset or framed under its parent, so that the reader sees the tree.

qualities.name: Grouping and rhythm
qualities.definition: Related items sit together and read as one group. Each group reads as one figure on its ground: a surface, a frame, a heading or space shows where it starts and ends. Each level of containment has its own treatment: the page holds cards with their own surface; a card holds groups with an inset, a hairline frame or space, not a second card. Inside a group, space separates the items first, then one hairline.

qualities.name: Feedback and state
qualities.definition: Each state uses its house pattern. A region wait is a skeleton with the box of the loaded state. A process wait is the teal loader. An empty state is a short title, one sentence and one primary control. An error is an inline alert with its cause and a next step. The layout holds at its edges: a long name, zero, one or many items, an error and a loading state keep the structure of the screen.

qualities.name: Consistency
qualities.definition: The same meaning has the same pattern on every screen, and a different meaning has a different pattern. The change reuses the house primitives and patterns: one corner radius (rounded-md), the button variants, the status pill, the alert. No new font, hex color, corner treatment, shadow or card style.

qualities.name: Brand fit
qualities.definition: The surface reads as the ctxpipe Operate UI: dark zinc floor, white primary, teal accent, Geist type, monospace for ids, paths, hashes and counts. Large type and atmosphere stay on onboarding.

qualities.name: Visual balance
qualities.definition: Space is spread evenly across a row and a column. No element sits close to one neighbor while a large empty gap stays on its other side, and a moved element leaves no lopsided gap. Judge the balance of the whole composition, not only one element.

qualities.name: Density
qualities.definition: Operate density, as in chat, connectors and settings: tight, not landing-page air. Forms and prose keep a maximum width; data surfaces are full width.

qualities.name: Restraint
qualities.definition: No generic AI decoration: no gradient, gradient text, glass, grain, glow or grid on product chrome, no hero type, no four equal KPI tiles, no teal on every row, no badge stacked above a title, no numbers on sections that are not a sequence, no icon tile above the heading of an empty state, no glow or drop shadow on hover. A colored edge on one side of a block marks a state, such as a block that needs the user, and is then the one signal of that block; a colored stripe that marks no state is decoration. An in-page card has no hard offset shadow and no wide black shadow; a dialog, popover, menu or toast keeps its house shadow. A blurred backdrop behind a modal, an uppercase heading that names a page section, and a status dot with its word are not decoration. These ctxpipe signatures are not tells: the mono uppercase .ctx-label as a section label in a dense panel (not as an eyebrow above a page title or a card heading), and corner crosses on a hero or summary card.
